designs.question: N38-N40: where `runtime` may be written (a parameter, a local, a field, a class type), with one meaning and one placement of the check for each; and what a value word (`owns`, `copy of`, `shares`, `weakref`, `ref mut`) covers in a call's argument and on the right of `=`.
designs.angle: SPEED AND SIMPLICITY FIRST: the shape a careful C programmer would choose, with the fewest bytes, compares and words, as long as the three goals hold.

shape.name: `runtime` on the name the call goes through; one binding everywhere, and `owns` is never an operand
shape.summary: N38/N39: `runtime` is a word on a NAME, never a type word. It is written after the `:` of a parameter or of a local declared with its type, before `dyn` (under any owner word) or before an `open`/`abstract` class name: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`, `fn show(a: runtime A):`, `q: runtime owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])`. One meaning in all three places: a `dyn` or `virtual` call through that name whose result points into an argument for some kinds and not others is not refused when compiling; the line that would be unsafe loads the fact `[LT-22]` records (one bit per source parameter, one for `this`) from the called method's entry in the value's kind's table (the interface table for a `dyn` value, the class's type table slot for a `virtual` method, `[OBJ-2]`/`[DSP-2]`) and does one bit test. The word is not part of the type, does not travel with the value (`show(q)` gives a plain `dyn Picker`), and is never on a field, a result type, a type argument or a capture (`E0100`, help: name the value with `runtime` in the function that calls through it); before a type whose kind is known when compiling it is `E2114`. A `virtual` call on `this` has no word of its own: the help is a parameter that says `runtime`, called with `this`. N40: keep ONE binding for every value word everywhere (today's `unary := value_word unary`), so the word always stands directly on the value it acts on, and close the one silent trap that binding has with a zero-cost refusal: an `owns` expression that is an operand of an operator is `E0121` (`owns i * 7` is `(owns i) * 7`, which would end `i` and multiply what it held; an operator reads its operands in place, §IV.9, so `owns` there can hand nothing over). Computed arguments take brackets, `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)`, as the compiler builds today (N42).
shape.rule_text:
**Part VII, `[LT-48]`.** Replace the heading and first sentence "**`runtime`: a `dyn` parameter's kind checked while the program runs.** `runtime` before a parameter's `dyn` type lets the function do what one of the kinds that may reach it would make unsafe (`[LT-1]`), where which kind it is is known only while the program runs: at the line that would be unsafe the function reads, from the table of the value's kind, which of the called method's parameters its result may point into, and stops the program there when the result may point into what the line changes." and the last two sentences "Where the kind is known when compiling, the word changes nothing: given `show(Yours(items=[9]))`, `show` is refused at `xs.push(owns 3)` when compiling, as without it (`E3021`). `runtime` is a word only after a parameter's `:` before `dyn` (`[LEX-15]`); it costs one load and one bit test at each line it guards (§X.4)." with:

* `[LT-48]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* **`runtime`: the kind of the name a call goes through, checked while the program runs.** `runtime` is written on a parameter or on a local declared with its type, after the `:` and before `dyn` (under any owner word: `dyn I`, `ref dyn I`, `owns dyn I`, `shares dyn I`, `shares mut dyn I`) or before the name of an `open` or `abstract` class: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`; `fn show(a: runtime A):` for `open class A`; `q: runtime owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])`; `a: runtime A = B() if input() == "b" else C()`. It has one meaning wherever it stands: a `dyn` or `virtual` call through that name, whose result points into an argument for some of the kinds that may reach the name and not for others (`[LT-1]`), is not refused when compiling where which kind it is is known only while the program runs; at the line that would be unsafe the function reads, from the called method's entry in the table of the value's kind (an interface's table for a `dyn` value, the class's type table for a `virtual` method, `[OBJ-2]`, `[DSP-2]`), whether the result may point into what the line changes, and stops the program there when it may. That fact is the one `[LT-22]` records for each implementation and each override (one bit per source parameter and one for `this`, in as many words as they need), kept in the method's entry of the kind's table, so a kind declared in another package, which the function's own package never saw, is checked as any other; a compare of kind identities instead would let such a kind through. The kinds that may reach a parameter are what its callers give it; those that may reach a local are what the function's own lines give it, followed through names and calls as `[LT-1]` says. `runtime` is a word on the name, not part of its type: the name's type is the type written after it, the value is given on with no word (`show(q)` for `fn show(p: dyn Picker):`, which then decides its own lines), and a function that calls through a name of its own says `runtime` on that name. With `[LT-1]`'s `Picker`, `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):` and `p: dyn Picker = Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else Yours(items=[9])`, `show(p)` prints `[9]` for a `Mine`, and for a `Yours` stops at `xs.push(owns 3)`: "panic at main.em:17:5: `xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `p` is a `Yours`, whose `pick` gives back the list it was handed". The local `q` above, with `r = q.pick(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 3)`, `println(r)` in the same function, stops the same way, naming `q`. With `open class A` whose `virtual fn first(other: Array[int]) -> Span[int]` returns `this.items` and `class B(A)` whose `override` returns `other`, `fn show(a: runtime A):` doing `r = a.first(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 2)`, `println(r)` prints for an `A` and stops for a `B`: "`xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `a` is a `B`, whose `first` gives back the list it was handed". Where the kind is known when compiling, the word changes nothing: given `show(Yours(items=[9]))` or `show(B())`, `show` is refused at the change when compiling, as without it (`E3021`). Without the word, `E3021`'s help names the one line to write: for a parameter, "to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`"; for a local, "to check it while running, write `runtime` where `q` is declared: `q: runtime owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == \"m\" else owns Yours(items=[9])`" (the declaration line written out, with its type where the program left it to be inferred); for a `virtual` call on `this` in a method of an open class, which has no name of its own to carry the word, "to check it while running, call through a parameter that says `runtime`: `fn show(a: runtime A):`, called `show(this)`"; for a value with no name (`ps[0].pick(xs)`, `this.picker.pick(xs)`), "to check it while running, name the value with `runtime` and call through the name: `p: runtime ref dyn Picker = ref ps[0]`". `runtime` is written nowhere else. Before a type whose kind is known when compiling (a struct, an enum, a final class, a list, a number) it is `E2114` ("`Circle` is a final class, so a `Circle` is always a `Circle`; remove `runtime`: `c: Circle`"); on a field, a result type, a type argument or a capture it is `E0100` ("`runtime` goes on the parameter or the local that is called through, not on a field; in the method that calls through `picker`, name its value first: `p: runtime ref dyn Picker = ref this.picker`"). It is a word only after the `:` of a parameter or of a local declared with its type (`[LEX-15]`); it costs one load and one bit test at each line it guards (§X.4).

**Part VII, `[LT-1]`.** Replace "with the help \"to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`\"), unless the parameter says `runtime` (`[LT-48]`)." with: "with the help `[LT-48]` gives for the name the call goes through (for a parameter, \"to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`\"), unless that name says `runtime` (`[LT-48]`). A `virtual` call on a class value (`fn show(a: A):` for an `open class A`, `r = a.first(xs)`), and a call through a local whose kind the function itself chooses while running (`q: owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == \"m\" else owns Yours(items=[9])`, then `r = q.pick(xs)` in the same function), are decided by the code of each kind and refused the same way, the message naming the class (\"`a` may be a `B`\") or the local (\"`q` may be a `Yours`\")."

**Part III, grammar (III.2 and III.4).** Replace `param         := [param_word] IDENT ":" ["runtime"] type ["..."] ["=" expression]   -- `Ts...`: the pack's values; `runtime` before a `dyn` type only ([LT-48])` with the same production whose comment reads `-- `Ts...`: the pack's values; `runtime` before `dyn` or an open class ([LT-48])`; replace `var_decl      := IDENT ":" type ["=" expr_list]` with `var_decl      := IDENT ":" ["runtime"] type ["=" expr_list]   -- `runtime` before `dyn` or an open class ([LT-48])`.

**Part II, `[LEX-15]`.** Replace "`runtime` after a parameter's `:` and directly before `dyn` (`[LT-48]`);" with "`runtime` after the `:` of a parameter or of a local declared with its type, directly before the type (`[LT-48]`);".

**Part VIII, `[DSP-2]`.** Replace "* `[DSP-2]` A virtual call loads its slot from the object's type table; slots are assigned in declaration order, base first, and an `override` reuses the base's slot." with:

* `[DSP-2]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* A virtual call loads its slot from the object's type table; slots are assigned in declaration order, base first, and an `override` reuses the base's slot. A slot's entry holds, beside the method's code, the fact `[LT-22]` records for the method that fills it (which of its source parameters, and whether `this`, its result may point into), read by a `runtime` check (`[LT-48]`); a slot a subclass does not override keeps the base's entry whole. The entry is written by the package that compiles the method, which has its body.

**Part X, §X.4 table.** Replace the row "| A `runtime dyn` parameter's check | guaranteed present | one load and one bit test, of the fact in the kind's method table, at each line the check guards, only where a kind that may reach the parameter makes the line unsafe (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling |" with "| A `runtime` name's check | guaranteed present | one load and one bit test, of the fact in the called method's entry of the value's kind's table (an interface's table; a class's type table for a `virtual` method, the same line the slot load reads, `[DSP-2]`), at each line the check guards, only where a kind that may reach the name makes the line unsafe (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling, and none at the call itself |".

**§XVII.9 registry.** `E3021` row: replace "(help: `runtime` on the parameter)" with "(help: `runtime` on the parameter or the local the call goes through, `[LT-48]`)". `E2114` row: replace "a type word that cannot apply to its type: `owns` on a class type (it always has its own block); `using` after a type with no heap memory of its own" with "a type word that cannot apply to its type: `owns` on a class type (it always has its own block); `using` after a type with no heap memory of its own; `runtime` before a type whose kind is known when compiling", rules add `[LT-48]`. `E0100` row: append ", and `runtime` on a field, a result type, a type argument or a capture (whose message gives the local to declare in the function that calls through it)", rules add `[LT-48]`.

---

**Part III, `[GRM-43]`.** Replace "stand before the value they act on and bind as a prefix `-` does: `snapshot = copy of items`, `other = shares mut items`, `cam.target = weakref player`, `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`, `boss = ref mut enemies[0]`, `bump(ref mut a)`, `blend(const ref mut d, s)`." with: "stand before the value they act on and bind as a prefix `-` does, wherever they stand, in a call's argument and on the right of `=` as anywhere else, so that the word is always directly before the value it acts on: `snapshot = copy of items`, `other = shares mut items`, `cam.target = weakref player`, `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`, `boss = ref mut enemies[0]`, `bump(ref mut a)`, `blend(const ref mut d, s)`, `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)` and `tx.send(owns (i * i))` (the brackets say the product is what is handed over, `[GRM-47]`), `q = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == \"m\" else owns Yours(items=[9])` (each branch says its word). `owns i ** 2` is `owns (i ** 2)`, as `-i ** 2` is `-(i ** 2)` (row 17)." Also mark the bullet *(changed in 0.9.20)*, and in the precedence table's row 16 note append "; `owns (i * 7)` hands the product over (`[GRM-47]`)".

**Part III, new bullet after `[GRM-43]`:**

* `[GRM-47]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **`owns` is never an operand.** An operator reads its operands in place (`Add.add(a, b)`, §IV.9), so `owns` before one of them hands nothing to the operator and only ends the name: `owns i * 7` is `(owns i) * 7`, which ends `i` and multiplies what it held. An `owns` expression that is an operand of an operator of rows 4 to 17 of the table (`or` to `**`), of `as`, of `in` or of a range's end, with or without brackets of its own, is `E0121`, whose message gives the line to write: in an argument, "`owns i * 7` is `(owns i) * 7`: `i` would be handed over before the multiplication, and the product is a new value; write `owns (i * 7)`: `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)`"; on the right of `=`, "`owns n * 2` is `(owns n) * 2`: `n` would end before the multiplication, and `=` hands the product over with no word; write `b = n * 2`". The other words stay as they are: before an operand each makes what it makes and ends nothing (`copy of a + b` adds a copy of `a` to `b`).

**Part V, `[FN-2a]`.** After "`take(owns [1, 2])` a list made in the call," insert "`m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)` a value computed in the call, in brackets (`[GRM-43]`, `[GRM-47]`),"; and after the `E3028` message for `take(xs)` insert: "for a computed argument, \"`insert` takes this argument over (its first line says `owns key: K`); say so at the call: write `owns` before it\", help `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)`". Mark *(changed in 0.9.20)*.

**§XVII.9 registry, new row:** | `E0121` | `owns` before an operand of an operator (`owns i * 7`, `(owns n) * 2`, `owns i as u8`, `-owns i`) | `[GRM-47]`, `[GRM-43]` |
shape.refuses:
(1) `runtime` on a field:

```ember
class Scene:
    picker: runtime owns dyn Picker
```
error[E0100]: `runtime` goes on the parameter or the local that is called through, not on a field; in the method that calls through `picker`, name its value first: `p: runtime ref dyn Picker = ref this.picker`

(2) `runtime` before a type whose kind is known when compiling: `fn area(c: runtime Circle) -> float:` → error[E2114]: `Circle` is a final class, so a `Circle` is always a `Circle`; remove `runtime`: `c: Circle`

(3) A kind the compiler can see stays refused, word or not (verdict 152): `fn show(a: runtime A):` with `show(B())` → error[E3021] at `xs.push(owns 2)`: `xs` changes while `r` may still look at it: `a` is a `B`, whose `first` gives back the list it was handed.

(4) N40: `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)` → error[E0121]: `owns i * 7` is `(owns i) * 7`: `i` would be handed over before the multiplication, and the product is a new value; write `owns (i * 7)`: `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)`. And `b = owns n * 2` → error[E0121]: `owns n * 2` is `(owns n) * 2`: `n` would end before the multiplication, and `=` hands the product over with no word; write `b = n * 2`. (Today `b = owns n * 2` compiles, ends `n`, and the later use of `n` is a puzzling `E3040` pointing at this line.)
shape.accepts:
N39, refused today with no help (`E3021` "`q` may be a `Yours`"):

```ember
fn main():
    q: runtime owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])
    xs = [1, 2]
    r = q.pick(xs)
    xs.push(owns 3)
    println(r)
```
prints `[9]` for a `Mine`; for a `Yours`: `panic at main.em:5:5: `xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `q` is a `Yours`, whose `pick` gives back the list it was handed`.

N38, refused today with no help ("`a` may be a `B`"):

```ember
fn show(a: runtime A):
    xs = [1]
    r = a.first(xs)
    xs.push(owns 2)
    println(r)

fn main():
    a: A = B() if input() == "b" else A()
    show(a)
```
prints `[7]` for an `A`; stops at `xs.push(owns 2)` for a `B`. The other angle (`runtime` as a type word) would accept the field form `picker: runtime owns dyn Picker`; this shape does not, and the function that pays writes the word on its own line instead.

N40: `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)`, `tx.send(owns (i * i))`, `b = n * 2`, and the two-branch `q = owns Mine(...) if ... else owns Yours(...)` all compile, each `owns` directly on the value it hands over.
shape.cost: Nothing runs for N40: `[GRM-47]` is a compile-time refusal; no §X.4 row changes. For N38/N39, exactly the row that exists, widened to the name: "| A `runtime` name's check | guaranteed present | one load and one bit test, of the fact in the called method's entry of the value's kind's table (an interface's table; a class's type table for a `virtual` method, the same line the slot load reads, `[DSP-2]`), at each line the check guards, only where a kind that may reach the name makes the line unsafe (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling, and none at the call itself |". Bytes: one fact word beside each interface-table entry (already the case since H.51) and beside each `virtual` slot: 8 bytes per slot per class, in read-only data, on the cache line the slot load already touches; a method with more than 63 source parameters uses a second word. Compares: the one bit test, at the guarded line only; a program with no `runtime` name pays zero; a `runtime` name whose kinds the compiler can see pays zero (the check is not emitted). No per-object byte, no header change, no count.
shape.build: Package compile: the parser accepts `runtime` after `:` on a `param` and on a `var_decl` (one token, contextual, `[LEX-15]`); the type checker keeps, per body, the set of names marked `runtime` (today's `runtime_params`, plus locals), refuses `E2114` where the type after it is not `dyn ...` or an open/abstract class, and `E0100` elsewhere (fields, result types, type arguments, captures). The borrow check runs per instance of kinds as today (`dyn_kinds`): a local's kinds are the union of what the body assigns to it, a parameter's what the instance's callers give; where a change of a place viewed only by the result of a call through a `runtime` name would be `E3021` for some kinds and not others, it emits a guard instead of the error: `fact = *(table->entries[slot].fact)`; `if (fact & (1 << j)) panic(msg)` — `table` is the fat pointer's table for a `dyn` value, or the object header's type table for a class value (`[OBJ-2]`); `slot` and the bit `j` (the argument's source-parameter index, or the `this` bit) are compile-time constants. Each package writes the fact word beside the code pointer in every interface-table entry and every `virtual` slot of the classes and implementations it compiles, straight from `[LT-22]`'s summary of that body; a subclass copies the base's entry for a slot it does not override. Nothing new goes into interface files: callers in other packages keep reading the worst case for a function's own `dyn` calls (unchanged), and the fact for a foreign kind is in that kind's table at run time, which is why the check is a bit test and not a kind compare. Link: tables are plain read-only data; no fixups, no registry. Run: only the guarded lines execute the load and the test; `[DSP-5]` devirtualisation (one reachable implementation) means a known kind and no guard. For N40 the parser is unchanged (`unary := value_word unary`); the walk that already finds `E0109` adds one check: an `owns` node whose parent is a binary, comparison, `as`, range, `in`, or prefix `-`/`~`/`not` node is `E0121`, before the call-word check (`E3028`), so a line gets one error; `E3028`'s help for a computed argument prints the brackets, as N42 builds today.
shape.owner_verdicts: Verdict 152 (JOB.md): the owner chose, of three placements (the making line, the call, the parameter), the parameter: "go with 3, keep runtime". This ruling keeps the parameter and does not move the word to the call; it adds the local's declaration line only for a call made in the same function (N39), where no parameter exists and the declaration is the only line that names the thing called through — the same principle (the function whose line pays writes the word on the name it calls through), but a reader of verdict 152 could call the N39 placement "the making line", so the owner should see it: marked touches_owner_verdict 152. Verdict 151 (per-kind checking) is kept and extended to class values and locals without change of meaning. Verdict 147 (`owns` at the call) is untouched by N40: `m.insert(owns (i * 7), owns i)` says `owns` at the call; verdict 157's two `runtime` messages are kept word for word for the parameter case.

designs.against_the_other_angle: The readability-first angle would take the lead's leaning on both questions, and both shapes cost more than they say. N38/N39 — `runtime` as a type word, allowed "in any declared type" (fields, result types, `Array[runtime owns dyn Pool]`): either `runtime dyn I` is a distinct type from `dyn I`, and every coercion of `[TYP-5]`, every generic instance, every interface file and every `copy of`/hand-over must say what happens to the word, or it is the same type and the word is a property the compiler must carry through fields, lists and returns into functions in other packages that never wrote it — a run-time check placed in a function by a line far from it, in another file, which is exactly the cost-visibility the X.4 goal forbids ("nothing runs unless the program says so") and the readability goal forbids (the reader of the paying line sees no word). A field also has no line of its own that is guarded, so "where the check is placed" has no answer for it; the name-based shape has one answer for all three places (the name the call goes through, in the function whose line pays) and needs no new type, no interface-file change and no layout change beyond the fact word H.51 already introduced for interface tables. N40 — a value word that "covers the whole expression" when first in an argument or first after `=`, and binds as a prefix elsewhere: that is two bindings for one word, chosen by position; the word stops standing on the thing it acts on (`owns i * 7` has `owns` on `i` and acts on the product, against the owner's rule "point at the word in the line that says what it is"); the question's own example `owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])` then reads as one `owns` covering the whole conditional with a nested prefix `owns` inside it, where today each branch says its word; `a, b = owns x, y` needs a comma rule; `f(1 + owns i * 7)` keeps the trap the special case was meant to remove; and the parser, the formatter and the editor must all know an `arg` and the right side of `=` from an `expression`. One binding plus `[GRM-47]` removes the trap in every position at no run-time cost, keeps E3028's help (`owns (i * 7)`) a line that compiles under either reading, and leaves the grammar as the compiler builds it (N42). The brackets cost the writer two characters and tell the reader, with no rule to remember, that the product is what is handed over.
designs.open_risks: (1) The help line `p: runtime ref dyn Picker = ref this.picker` for an `owns dyn` field relies on `ref` of an `owns dyn I` place giving a `ref dyn I` (the compiler's MIR does `&(*b.0)` today, and p04 line 782 names `ref dyn I` as a view's type); `[TYP-5]`/`[TYP-14]` should be checked to say that coercion in words, or the help must print the type the compiler infers. (2) A `runtime` local replaced through a `ref mut` view (`mem.swap(ref mut q, ref mut q2)`) is "not followed" in the lead's design and gets the worst case for which kinds reach it; safety is unaffected (the check reads the value's own table at the line), but the rule text should say the kind set then is every kind of the table, as the design does. (3) `show(this)` as the help for a `virtual` call on `this` gives `this` to a plain class parameter, which reads the object (`[FN-9]`); a method that also changes `this` after that call is fine, but the help must not be given where `show` would need `ref mut a: A` — the compiler should print `ref mut` when the guarded lines change the object. (4) `[DSP-5]` and the vtable fact: a slot's entry must be the same shape in every unit (code pointer + fact word); `[ABI-1]`/`[RT-*]` may need one sentence for the entry layout if hot reload copies tables. (5) `[GRM-47]`'s list of operators (rows 4 to 17, `as`, `in`, a range end) should be cross-checked against `[GRM-16]`'s wording for `E0107` (a jump as an operand), which it mirrors. (6) Verdict 152's "go with 3" over the making line: the owner may read the N39 local placement as the rejected option 1 and should confirm; if refused, N39 falls back to "move the lines into a function with a `runtime` parameter", which this ruling's help already gives for `this` and would then give for a local too. (7) `E0121` is a new code (E0119 is also free); `[DIA-6]` needs its page and `codes.rs`'s registry test the row.

designs.question: N38-N40: where `runtime` may be written (a parameter, a local, a field, a class type) with one meaning and one placement of the check (`[LT-48]`, `[LT-1]`, `[DSP-2]`, `[DSP-5]`); and what a value word (`owns`, `copy of`, `shares`, `weakref`, `ref mut`, ...) covers when written before a computed value (`[GRM-15]`, `[GRM-43]`, `[FN-2a]`, `[OWN-9]`, `[OWN-13]`).
designs.angle: Safety and separate compilation first: the shape Rust's designers would choose, proven when compiling, holding for a package compiled once and used by programs it never saw, as long as the three goals hold.

shape.name: `runtime` is a word of a declared type, read at the call; a value word is the head of a given value, never an operator
shape.summary: N38/N39: `runtime` is written in the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field, directly before `dyn` or before an `open`/`abstract` class's name, after any holding word (`p: runtime dyn Picker`, `q: owns runtime dyn Picker`, `a: runtime A`, `pools: Array[owns runtime dyn Pool]`). One meaning everywhere: a call on a value reached through that declaration whose result is a view reads, AT THE CALL, the called method's fact (`[LT-22]`'s bits: which parameters and `this` the result may point into) from the entry of the value's kind's own table (the interface table for `dyn`, the virtual slot of the class's type table for a class value), keeps it with the view, and at each later changing line `[LT-1]` could not decide tests one bit and stops the program. The fact travels in the kind's table with a width its declaration fixes, so a subclass or implementation in a package the function never saw is checked as any other, and no per-program list of kinds is needed. A view that leaves the function is the worst case, checked when compiling. `runtime` is no part of the type's identity. N40: the value words are taken out of the `unary` production. A value word stands first in a GIVEN VALUE (an argument, each value after `=`, a constructor's field value, `return`'s value, a `for`'s iterable, a `match`'s scrutinee, a literal's element/key/value, a lambda's `=>` body, and each branch or arm of a conditional or `match` expression standing there) and covers all of it: `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)`, `tx.send(owns i * i)`, `b = owns n * 2`, `owns Mine(...) if c else owns Yours(...)` with a word on each branch. Anywhere else (an operand, brackets that are not a call's, a condition) a value word is `E0119`. One binding, not two; nothing accepted today is refused except operand forms the text never gave a meaning (`(owns i) * 7`, `1 + owns n`).

## N38/N39: `runtime`

* `[LT-48]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replaces the whole bullet. Sentences replaced: "**`runtime`: a `dyn` parameter's kind checked while the program runs.**"; "`runtime` before a parameter's `dyn` type lets the function do what one of the kinds that may reach it would make unsafe (`[LT-1]`), where which kind it is is known only while the program runs: at the line that would be unsafe the function reads, from the table of the value's kind, which of the called method's parameters its result may point into, and stops the program there when the result may point into what the line changes."; "That fact is the one `[LT-22]` records for each implementation (one bit per source parameter and one for `this`), kept in the method's entry of the kind's table, so a kind declared in another package, which the function's own package never saw, is checked as any other; a compare of kind identities instead would let such a kind through."; "`runtime` is a word only after a parameter's `:` before `dyn` (`[LEX-15]`); it costs one load and one bit test at each line it guards (§X.4)." New text:

  * `[LT-48]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* **`runtime`: a kind checked while the program runs.** `runtime` is written in a declared type, directly before `dyn` or before the name of an `open` or `abstract` class, after any holding word, on a parameter, a local or a field, at any depth of the type (`p: runtime dyn Picker`, `q: owns runtime dyn Picker`, `a: runtime A`, `boss: shares mut runtime Enemy`, `pools: Array[owns runtime dyn Pool]`; `[GRM-47]`). It has one meaning wherever it stands. A call on a value reached through that declaration (the name, or a field or element of it) whose result is a view, or that puts a view in through `ref mut` (`[LT-47]`), may be one `[LT-1]` would refuse for a kind that may reach the value, where which kind it is is known only while the program runs. The function then reads, at the call, from the entry of the called method in the table of the value's kind, which of the method's parameters its result may point into (the fact `[LT-22]` records for each implementation and each override: one bit per source parameter, one for `this`, and one per `ref mut` parameter a view may be put into), keeps it with the view, and at each later line that changes a place the view may point into for one of those kinds, while the view is still used, tests the bit for that place and stops the program when it is set: "panic at main.em:17:5: `xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `p` is a `Yours`, whose `pick` gives back the list it was handed" (the value named as the call writes it, `this.pools[k]`; the kind as the compiler shows types). The fact lives in the kind's own table — the interface's table of the kind for a `dyn` value (`[DSP-3]`), the virtual slot of the class's type table for a class value (`[DSP-2]`) — with a width the method's declaration fixes, so a kind declared in a package the function's own package never saw is checked as any other; a compare of kind identities instead would let such a kind through. With `[LT-1]`'s `Picker`, `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):` and `p: dyn Picker = Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else Yours(items=[9])`, `show(p)` prints `[9]` for a `Mine` and for a `Yours` stops at `xs.push(owns 3)`. Inside one function it is the same: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])`, then `r = q.pick(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 3)`, `println(r)`, prints `[9]` for a `Mine` and stops at `xs.push(owns 3)` for a `Yours`. For a class, with `open class A` whose `virtual fn first(other: Array[int]) -> Span[int]` returns `this.items` and `class B(A)` whose `override` returns `other`, `fn show(a: runtime A):` doing `r = a.first(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 2)`, `println(r)` prints for an `A` and stops for a `B`: "panic at main.em:14:5: `xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `a` is a `B`, whose `first` gives back the list it was handed". Where the kind is known when compiling, the word changes nothing: given `show(Yours(items=[9]))` or `show(B())`, `show` is refused at the changing line when compiling, as without it (`E3021`). A view the word checks that leaves the function — returned, stored in a field or a list, kept by a call, captured by a function value — carries no fact (`[LT-30]`): it is taken to point into every argument the kinds may make it point into, as without the word, and its users are checked when compiling (`[LT-1]` rule 3). `runtime` is no part of the type: `runtime dyn Picker` and `dyn Picker` have one layout and one identity, a value passes between them with nothing written, and a function the value reaches checks its own parameters by its own first line. Before a type with one kind (a struct, an enum, a class neither `open` nor `abstract`, `some I`, a number) it is `E2114` ("a `Point` value has one kind, so there is nothing to check while running; remove `runtime`: `p: Point`"); anywhere but the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field (a result type, a function type, a bound, a cast, a kind test, an alias) it is `E0100` ("`runtime` belongs to the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field; write it where `q` is declared: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = ...`"). It costs one load at the call and one bit test at each line it guards, and nothing where no line needs it (§X.4).

* `[GRM-47]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **`runtime` in a type.** `runtime` stands directly before `dyn` or before a class's name, after any holding word (`owns`, `shares`, `shares mut`, `thread_shared`, `weakref`, `ref`, `ref mut`), in the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field, at any depth (`q: owns runtime dyn Picker`, `pools: Array[owns runtime dyn Pool]`, `a: runtime A`); what it means is `[LT-48]`'s. A local declared without a type has nowhere to carry it, so the help writes the declaration with its type. Grammar: replace `param := [param_word] IDENT ":" ["runtime"] type ["..."] ["=" expression]   -- `Ts...`: the pack's values; `runtime` before a `dyn` type only ([LT-48])` with `param := [param_word] IDENT ":" type ["..."] ["=" given]   -- `Ts...`: the pack's values`, and add to `base_type` the alternative `| "runtime" ("dyn" bound_list | path_type)   -- in a parameter's, local's or field's type only ([GRM-47], [LT-48])`.

* `[LT-1]` *(changed in 0.9.9)* *(changed in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace: "with the help \"to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`\"), unless the parameter says `runtime` (`[LT-48]`)." with: "with the help naming the declaration the value was reached through: for a parameter \"to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(p: runtime dyn Picker):`\"; for a local \"to check it while running, write `runtime` in `q`'s type: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == \"m\" else owns Yours(items=[9])`\"; for a field \"to check it while running, write `runtime` in the field's type: `pools: Array[owns runtime dyn Pool]`\"; for a class value the kind named is the class, \"`a` may be a `B`\"), unless that declaration says `runtime` (`[LT-48]`)."

* `[LEX-15]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace "`runtime` after a parameter's `:` and directly before `dyn` (`[LT-48]`);" with "`runtime` in a declared type directly before `dyn` or a class's name (`[GRM-47]`, `[LT-48]`);".

* `[DSP-2]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — append: "Each slot holds, beside the override's code, the fact `[LT-22]` records for that override, in the width the base's declaration fixes (`[LT-48]`)." `[DSP-3]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — append: "Each entry of an interface's table holds the implementation's fact the same way, and the table ends with the kind's qualified name, which a `runtime` stop prints (`[LT-48]`)."

* `[COST-3]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace the row "| A `runtime dyn` parameter's check | guaranteed present | one load and one bit test, of the fact in the kind's method table, at each line the check guards, only where a kind that may reach the parameter makes the line unsafe (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling |" with "| A `runtime` check | guaranteed present | one load of the fact from the kind's table at a call on a value reached through a `runtime` declaration whose result is a view, and one bit test at each line that view guards, only where a kind that may reach the value makes the line unsafe and which kind it is is not known when compiling (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling, none at a call no guarded line follows, and none for a value whose declaration does not say `runtime` |".

* Registry (p17a-codes.md): `E3021` row, replace "(help: `runtime` on the parameter)" with "(help: `runtime` in the declaration the value was reached through: the parameter, the local or the field)"; `E2114` row, append "; `runtime` before a type with one kind" and `[LT-48]` to its rules; `E0100` row, append "and `runtime` outside the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field" with `[GRM-47]`. Glossary (p24-appx-f.md), new row: "| **`runtime`** | the word in a parameter's, local's or field's declared type, before `dyn` or a class's name, that has the value's kind checked while the program runs at a line `[LT-1]` cannot decide when compiling (`[LT-48]`) |". H.51: a bullet under "Holes in the memory-safety rules" after the `[LT-48]` one: "`runtime` is a word of any declared type that carries a kind — a parameter's, a local's, a field's, before `dyn` or a class's name — with one meaning and one check, read at the call that makes the view and tested at the line (`[LT-48]`, `[GRM-47]`, `[DSP-2]`, `[DSP-3]`, the `[COST-3]` row)."

## N40: what a value word covers

* `[GRM-43]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace "stand before the value they act on and bind as a prefix `-` does: `snapshot = copy of items`, `other = shares mut items`, `cam.target = weakref player`, `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`, `boss = ref mut enemies[0]`, `bump(ref mut a)`, `blend(const ref mut d, s)`." with: "stand first in a **given value** and cover the whole of it. A given value is a value a line gives to a place: an argument; each value after `=` in a declaration or an assignment; a constructor's field value; the value after `return`; the iterable of a `for` or of a comprehension's clause; the scrutinee of a `match`; an element, key or value of a list, set or map literal, or a comprehension's head; a lambda's `=>` body; and, inside a given value, each branch of a conditional expression and each arm's value of a `match` expression, each with its own word. So `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)` gives the map the number `i * 7` and then `i`; `tx.send(owns i * i)`; `b = owns n * 2` ends `n`; `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == \"m\" else owns Yours(items=[9])` says `owns` on each branch; `snapshot = copy of items`, `other = shares mut items`, `cam.target = weakref player`, `Watcher(target=sharedref mut players[r])`, `boss = ref mut enemies[0]`, `bump(ref mut a)`, `blend(const ref mut d, s)`. A value word is not an operator: written as an operand (`(owns i) * 7`, `1 + owns n`, `-owns n`), inside round brackets that are not a call's (`x = (owns n)`), or in a condition, it is `E0119` (\"`owns` here is an operand of `*`, which only computes with `i`; a value word stands first in the value given and covers all of it: `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)`\"; \"`owns` here is an operand of `+`, which only reads `n`; remove it: `x = 1 + n`\")." The rest of the bullet (`copy` and `of`, `sharedref`, `using`) stands. Grammar: replace `unary := ("-" | "~") unary | value_word unary | "cast" postfix_expr "as" type | power` with `unary := ("-" | "~") unary | "cast" postfix_expr "as" type | power`; add `given := [value_word] (lambda | or_expr ["if" or_expr "else" given])   -- a value given to a place ([GRM-43])` and `given_list := given {"," given} [","]`; replace `arg := expression | IDENT "=" expression | IDENT "..."` with `arg := given | IDENT "=" given | IDENT "..."`; `var_decl := IDENT ":" type ["=" expr_list]` with `["=" given_list]`; `assignment := target_list "=" expr_list` with `"=" given_list`; `jump_expr := "return" [expr_list] | ...` with `"return" [given_list] | ...`; `for_stmt := "for" for_target "in" expression ":"` with `"in" given ":"`; `match_stmt := "match" expression ":"` and `match_expr := "match" expression ":" ... "=>" expression` with `given` in both places; in `list_lit`, `map_lit`, `set_lit` and `comprehension` each `expression` element, key, value or head with `given`; `lambda ... ("=>" expression | ":" block)` with `("=>" given | ":" block)`; `comp_clauses := "for" for_target "in" or_expr ...` with `"in" [value_word] or_expr` (a clause's `if` is its filter, so no conditional stands there). Precedence table row 16: replace "`-` `~` · `ref` `ref mut` `const ref mut` `copy of` `owns` `shares` `shares mut` `thread_shared` `weakref` `sharedref mut` · `cast … as` (prefix) | `-x as u8` is `(-x) as u8`; `ref a.b[i]` names `a.b[i]`; `copy of xs[0]` copies `xs[0]`" with "`-` `~` · `cast … as` (prefix) | `-x as u8` is `(-x) as u8`; the value words are not operators: each stands first in a given value and covers all of it (`[GRM-43]`): `ref a.b[i]` names `a.b[i]`, `owns i * 7` is the number `i * 7`".

* `[GRM-36]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace "`ref` binds like unary minus: `ref a.b[i]` names `a.b[i]`." with "`ref` covers the whole given value, which must be a place: `ref a.b[i]` names `a.b[i]`, and `ref a + b` is `E0111`."

* `[FN-2a]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — after "`take(owns [1, 2])` a list made in the call," insert "`m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)` a number computed in the call (the word covers the whole argument, `[GRM-43]`),".

* `[GRM-15]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — after "`take(owns [1, 2])`," insert "`tx.send(owns i * i)`,".

* `[OWN-13]` *(changed in 0.9.20)* — replace "Before a value, a word acts on the object the value names" with "A word stands first in a given value and covers all of it (`[GRM-43]`); it acts on the object the value names".

* Registry: new row "| `E0119` | a value word written as an operand, inside brackets that are not a call's, or anywhere but first in a given value | `[GRM-43]` |". Glossary: new row "| **given value** | a value a line gives to a place — an argument, what follows `=`, a constructor's field value, `return`'s value, a `for`'s iterable, a `match`'s scrutinee, a literal's element, a lambda's `=>` body, and each branch or arm standing there — whose first word, if any, is its value word and covers all of it (`[GRM-43]`) |". H.51, under "Words made consistent": "A value word is the head of a given value and covers all of it, never an operator (`[GRM-43]`, `[GRM-36]`, `[FN-2a]`, `[GRM-15]`, `[OWN-13]`, `E0119`), so `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)` needs no brackets and `(owns i) * 7` is refused rather than left unsaid."

Refused at `xs.push(owns 2)`: E3021 "`xs` changes while `r` may still look at it: `a` may be a `B`, and which kind it is is only known while running", help "to check it while running, write `runtime` on the parameter: `fn show(a: runtime A):`". N39 (local): `q: owns dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])`, `r = q.pick(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 3)`, `println(r)`: E3021 "`xs` changes while `r` may still look at it: `q` may be a `Yours`, and which kind it is is only known while running", help "to check it while running, write `runtime` in `q`'s type: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])`". Misplaced word: `fn show(p: runtime Point):` is E2114 "a `Point` value has one kind, so there is nothing to check while running; remove `runtime`: `p: Point`"; `fn make() -> owns runtime dyn Picker:` is E0100 "`runtime` belongs to the declared type of a parameter, a local or a field; write it where `q` is declared: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = ...`". While running, with the word and a `B`: "panic at main.em:14:5: `xs` changes while `r` looks at it: `a` is a `B`, whose `first` gives back the list it was handed". N40: `m.insert((owns i) * 7, owns i)` is E0119 "`owns` here is an operand of `*`, which only computes with `i`; a value word stands first in the value given and covers all of it: `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)`"; `x = 1 + owns n` is E0119 "`owns` here is an operand of `+`, which only reads `n`; remove it: `x = 1 + n`"; `ref a + b` stays E0111.
shape.accepts: N38: the class program above with `fn show(a: runtime A):` compiles for `a: A = A() if input() == "a" else B()` (today: E3021 with no help, since `runtime` has no place before a class name); it prints for an `A` and stops with the message above for a `B`; `show(B())` with the kind visible stays E3021 when compiling (verdict 152 a). N39: `q: owns runtime dyn Picker = owns Mine(items=[9]) if input() == "m" else owns Yours(items=[9])` then `r = q.pick(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 3)`, `println(r)` in one `main` compiles (today refused with no way out but moving the lines into a function with a `runtime` parameter), prints `[9]` for a `Mine`, stops at `xs.push(owns 3)` for a `Yours`. A field: `pools: Array[owns runtime dyn Pool]` lets `fn pick(this, k: int, xs: Array[int])` do `r = this.pools[k].pick(xs)`, `xs.push(owns 3)`, `println(r)`, with the kind read from the element's table, a `Pool` implemented in a package this one never saw included. N40: `m.insert(owns i * 7, owns i)` and `tx.send(owns i * i)` compile with no brackets (today E3028 with the help `owns (i * 7)`, N42); `b = owns n * 2` ends `n`; `take(owns (i * 7))` still compiles (the brackets are an atom inside the given value). The other angle's prefix-minus binding accepts none of these without brackets.
shape.cost: N38/N39: while the program runs, only at a call on a value reached through a `runtime` declaration whose result is a view, and only where some kind that may reach it makes a later line unsafe and the kind is not known when compiling: one load of the fact word from the kind's table entry at the call (for a class value, off the same virtual slot the call already loads, `[DSP-2]`; for a `dyn` value, off the interface table entry the call already uses, `[DSP-3]`), held in a hidden local of the frame, and one `and` with a constant mask and one branch at each guarded line. Nothing where the kinds are known when compiling, nothing for a declaration without the word, nothing at a line no guarded view reaches, and nothing when a view leaves the function (then the worst case is checked when compiling). The stop reads the kind's name pointer from the table only on the failing path. The §X.4 row is rewritten as given in rule_text: "A `runtime` check | guaranteed present | one load of the fact from the kind's table at a call on a value reached through a `runtime` declaration whose result is a view, and one bit test at each line that view guards, only where a kind that may reach the value makes the line unsafe and which kind it is is not known when compiling (`[LT-48]`); none where the kinds are known when compiling, none at a call no guarded line follows, and none for a value whose declaration does not say `runtime`". N40: a grammar rule; nothing runs and no X.4 row changes (`owns` before a computed value puts the computed value where the parameter's words say, as `take(owns [1, 2])` does today).
shape.build: N38/N39, package compile: for each implementation of a `dyn`-usable interface method and each `virtual`/`override` body, the compiler already computes the `[LT-22]` summary; it encodes it as a bit vector (one bit per source parameter, one for `this`, one per `ref mut` parameter a view may be put into, `[LT-47]`) of a width the method's DECLARATION fixes (ceil((n+2)/64) words, the same in every package that sees the interface or base class), and writes it beside the code pointer in the kind's interface table entry (`[DSP-3]`) or virtual slot (`[DSP-2]`); the table ends with a pointer to the kind's qualified name for the stop. The interface artifact (`[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-2]`) records each implementation's bits so a dependant that emits its own per-unit copy of a table (N49) writes the same bits. The parser accepts `runtime` in `base_type` before `dyn` or a path type; name resolution marks the declaration (parameter position, local, field) and reports E2114 when the path names a type with one kind and E0100 when the `runtime` type sits anywhere but a parameter's, local's or field's declared type; `hir::Program::runtime_params` becomes `runtime_decls` (params, locals, fields). Borrow check: per kind set as today (`[LT-1]`, `dyn_kinds`). Where a `dyn` or virtual call's receiver was reached through a `runtime` declaration, the kind set has more than one member or is unknown, and a later line is unsafe for some member: no E3021; instead the lowering inserts, right after the call, a load of the entry's fact word (for a class value the slot is found through the object's type table exactly as the call found it; for `dyn`, the entry the call used) into a hidden local tied to the result view, live to the view's last use (`[BCK-2]`), and before the changing line `if fact & MASK != 0: panic(...)` with MASK the bits of the places the line changes (argument i, `this`), computed when compiling, and the message built from the kind's name pointer. A changing line reached from a view with no `runtime` origin keeps E3021. A view that is returned, stored, captured or kept by a callee gets its summary as `[LT-1]` rule 3 gives it (into every source), so callers are checked when compiling with no run-time fact. Link: nothing beyond today (tables are per unit; the bits come from the artifact). Run: the load and the test. A pub function in a library with a `runtime` parameter or field is compiled once; a program that passes it a kind from a third package is checked by the bits that package wrote in its own table. N40, parse: `given` is parsed at every given-value position (argument, after `=`, constructor field value, `return`, `for ... in`, `match`, literal elements, `=>` bodies, each branch of a conditional there); the parser peeks for a value word, attaches it to the given-value node, and parses the branch; `unary` no longer accepts a value word, so a word met where an operand is expected is E0119 naming the operator being parsed and the head of the enclosing given value in the help; a jump met at the head of a given value keeps E0107. The borrow check reads the call word from the argument node's head as it does today (N41), so `E3028`'s help becomes `owns i * 7` with no brackets; `ember fmt --migrate` (`[CLI-20]`) drops brackets that enclosed a whole argument after a value word and lists any line where a value word was followed by a binary operator, since its meaning moves.

designs.against_the_other_angle: The other angle (readability first, the lead's leaning taken whole) would take two shapes. On N40 it would keep the lead's split: a value word first in an argument or first after `=` covers the whole, elsewhere it binds as a prefix minus. That gives one word two grammars decided by where it sits in the line: `b = owns n * 2` covers `n * 2`, but `b = 1 + owns n * 2` is `1 + ((owns n) * 2)`, and `f(g(owns i * 7))` covers the whole only in the inner call — the reader must first find the position and then apply the right binding, which fails the readability test the angle is named for ("what does the line say the value is?" has two answers). It also keeps the prefix forms alive, and every one of them is a program nobody means: `(owns i) * 7` hands `i` to `*`, which only computes; `copy of s + t` copies then adds; the text then owes a meaning or an error for each, operator by operator (today they are unsaid, so `E0901`). Taking the words out of `unary` removes the whole class with one rule and one code, and what remains is exactly the owner's examples. A `dyn` or `virtual` call through that name whose result is a view, and which `[LT-1]` would refuse for some of the kinds that may reach the name and not for others, is not refused when compiling where which kind it is is known only while the program runs. The function then reads, at the call, from the called method's entry in the table of the value's kind (an interface's table for a `dyn` value, `[DSP-3]`; the method's slot in the class's type table for a `virtual` method, `[DSP-2]`), which of the method's parameters its result may point into, keeps that fact with the result for as long as the result is used, and at each later line that changes a place the result may point into for one of those kinds, while the result will still be used, tests the fact's bit for that place and stops the program when it is set. The fact is read once, at the call, so a name given another value between the call and the change (`q = owns Yours(items=[1])`) cannot name the wrong kind: that line is itself a change of what the result may point into for a kind whose result points into `this`, and is tested as any other. The fact is the one `[LT-22]` records for each implementation and each override: bit 0 for `this`, bit k for the method's k-th parameter in the order of its declaration, counted from 1, in one word of 64 bits and one more word for each further 64 parameters, the count taken from the interface's or the base class's declaration of the method, so that every package writes the entry in one shape; it is kept beside the code pointer in the method's entry of the kind's table, so a kind declared in another package, which the function's own package never saw, is checked as any other; a compare of kind identities instead would let such a kind through.
